articles.title: Patrick Mahomes can't hide reaction after Andy Reid broke news he's been working toward for months
articles.standfirst: Reid has cleared the three-time Super Bowl MVP to start
articles.summary: Reid has cleared the three-time Super Bowl MVP to start
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes didn't spend the offseason simply trying to become healthy enough to play again. He spent it trying to become himself again.

That mattered Thursday, when Kansas City Chiefs coach Andy Reid confirmed that Mahomes will start the season opener against the Denver Broncos , completing a long recovery from the torn ACL and LCL he suffered late last year.

“This has always been the goal, to get out there and play Week 1,” Mahomes said. “It was a long offseason. A lot of work, a lot of great people around me — trainers, Brittany, my family — supporting me, but now we get to go out there and play the sport that I love.”

He added that he was “super excited” to return at Arrowhead and face a strong Denver team.

Injury won't change who he is

The obvious concern is whether a quarterback coming off such a serious injury will be more cautious, particularly against a defense capable of pressuring him. Mahomes said that's not how he plans to approach it.

“You’ve got to go out there and be yourself,” he said. “I’ve built up the strength, I’ve built up all the days of rehab so I can be myself.”

He acknowledged that avoiding unnecessary punishment still matters, but made it clear that caution will not become hesitation.

“I’m going to keep myself out of harm’s way like I always will, not trying to take big hits and stuff like that, but I’m a competitor,” Mahomes added. “I signed up for this, and I’m going to go out there and play football.”

That mindset has always been central to Mahomes ’ game. His ability to extend plays, improvise and keep attacking has been as important to Kansas City’s success as his arm talent.

“Playing quarterback is one thing, but you’ve got to love competing to have success,” Mahomes stated. “I’m going to be myself.”

Reid gets version of Mahomes he wanted

Mahomes underwent surgery the day after the injury and attacked his rehabilitation aggressively enough to participate in offseason work and training camp.

He hasn't taken a live game snap since December, but he doesn't expect that absence to create a major psychological barrier.

“I think it’s going to be hard for me not to just be myself when I step on the field,” Mahomes said.

“Usually, you get hit once or twice and you’re kind of like, ‘Alright, I’ve got to go out there and play.’ I’m excited just to be out there on the field again with my teammates and try to find a way to get a win.”

That is probably the most encouraging part of the announcement for Kansas City. Reid isn't getting back a quarterback who sounds tentative about what comes next.

Mahomes is talking like someone who believes the rehab did what it was supposed to do. Week 1 was the target all along and now he gets to prove he's ready for it.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes walks away in anger as knee injury doubts overshadow Week 1 return
articles.standfirst: Patrick Mahomes is done answering questions about his injury.
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes is done answering questions about his injury.
articles.body:
A new season is getting closer for the Kansas City Chiefs , and it appears that Patrick Mahomes is ready to return. However, before Week 1 , the quarterback has made it clear that he wants to put all questions about his recovery behind him. The quarterback made it clear that he no longer wants to keep talking about his leg injury after a reporter asked him once again about his physical condition during his meeting with the media on Thursday.

“Hopefully I’m done with the questions about the leg,” he told reporters.

The three-time Super Bowl champion suffered tears to the ACL and LCL ligaments in his left knee during the matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers last December . The severity of the injury raised doubts about his availability for the start of the season, but after a successful surgery, the quarterback was cleared to return to practice in July.

From the moment he underwent surgery, Mahomes set Week 1 as his main goal, and everything indicates he will stay on track with his recovery timeline. The quarterback explained in August that doctors had projected a return nine months after surgery if he followed the proper rehabilitation process.

“It’s nine months. It’s the amount of time [doctors] said from the beginning, that if I did everything the right way, I would be ready to play Week One. I’m someone that, if you put [a goal] out in front of me, I want to go out and get it and maximize every single opportunity, every rep in the weight room, every hour that I can spend in the building to get my body right. This has always been the plan. From the day I got the surgery, as quick as I did, to hopefully the first game of the year, the plan will go accordingly, and I’ll be able to go out there and be myself.”

Head coach Andy Reid also confirmed that there is a strong possibility Mahomes will be the starter in the season opener against the Denver Broncos.

“As far as our roster goes, there's a very good chance that Patrick will go ahead and start unless something were to come up here in the next couple days,” Reid told reporters. “Most likely he'll be the guy that's out there.”

With their offensive centerpiece back, the Chiefs are looking to move past any uncertainty and begin a new season with their sights set on competing for another NFL championship.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $25 billion Chiefs boss gives everyone a lesson in humility
articles.standfirst: Clark Hunt could have watched from somewhere dry, but the billionaire Chiefs owner stood in the pouring rain
articles.summary: Clark Hunt could have watched from somewhere dry, but the billionaire Chiefs owner stood in the pouring rain
articles.body:
Clark Hunt could have sent someone else. The billionaire owner of the Kansas City Chiefs has employees, executives and an entire organization capable of distributing flags without him ever stepping into the rain.

Instead, Hunt stood outside a Kansas City-area McDonald’s early Thursday morning, getting soaked as he personally handed $5 Chiefs flags to fans alongside Pro Football Hall of Famer Bobby Bell. The simple moment quickly went viral because people are not accustomed to seeing someone connected to a $25 billion fortune doing an ordinary job in miserable weather.

The flags were part of the Chiefs’ annual Red Thursday fundraiser benefiting Ronald McDonald House Kansas City , which supports families with children receiving medical care. The limited-edition design featured Andy Reid’s famous phrase, “How ’Bout Those Chiefs,” with all proceeds remaining in the Kansas City community.

Clark Hunt understands the importance of being close to the people

The financial comparison makes the scene even more powerful. The Hunt family has an estimated net worth of $25.6 billion, although that number represents the entire family fortune and not Clark alone. Their wealth began with oil tycoon H.L. Hunt and later expanded through energy, real estate, hotels and professional sports.

Clark is the son of Chiefs founder Lamar Hunt and serves as the franchise’s chairman and CEO. He also leads Hunt Sports Group and is closely connected to FC Dallas and Major League Soccer. The Chiefs alone were recently valued at approximately $6.2 billion.

Hunt could spend his mornings inside private offices discussing billion-dollar stadiums, NFL television deals and the future of one of the league’s most recognizable franchises. On Thursday, however, the millionaire businessman was standing outside in the pouring rain and placing flags directly into the hands of ordinary fans.

That does not erase the enormous distance between Hunt’s life and theirs . But it does show that he understands something many wealthy owners sometimes forget: people want to see the person in charge. They want an owner who is willing to come close, look them in the eye and participate in the traditions they are asked to support.

Showing up was also smart leadership. Hunt knows the Chiefs are more than Travis Kelce, Patrick Mahomes, Super Bowl trophies or a valuable NFL business . The franchise depends on people who wear red, buy tickets, stand in bad weather and make the team part of their families.

Not many billionaire owners would personally hand out $5 flags in pouring rain. Clark Hunt did, and for one morning, one of America’s richest sports families offered everyone a small lesson in humility.

articles.title: Taylor Swift becomes an insect: Four new species bear her name
articles.standfirst: Swifties have another reason to celebrate: Taylor now has her own bugs
articles.summary: Swifties have another reason to celebrate: Taylor now has her own bugs
articles.body:
Taylor Swift has entered an unexpected new era: she’s now part of the scientific record. Researchers have named a newly established genus of Australian plant-feeding insects Swiftiephylus, giving the pop superstar an unusual place in entomology.

The genus contains four newly described species, all connected to Swift or her music.

The names include Swiftiephylus taylorae, Swiftiephylus amator, Swiftiephylus intrepidus and Swiftiephylus poetorum. Their Latin-inspired names reference Taylor, Lover, Fearless and poets, respectively.

The insects belong to the Miridae family, one of the largest families of true bugs, which contains thousands of described species worldwide.

The naming idea came from Sarah Schroeder , a doctoral researcher in entomology at the University of California, Riverside, and a lifelong Swift fan.

“It felt authentic to me as a lifelong Swiftie to honor Taylor in this way, as well as bring attention to the diversity of insects that has yet to be discovered,” said Schr o eder in a statement.

The insects have pale yellow bodies decorated with red accents, a combination Schroeder associated with Swift’s blonde hair and red lipstick. The insects are closely associated with Australian she-oaks, and their appearance could help them blend into the flowers and surrounding vegetation.

From forgotten specimens to scientific discovery

What makes the story especially remarkable is that these insects weren’t discovered during a recent expedition. Their specimens were collected during Australian biodiversity expeditions between 1995 and 2004, as part of a major effort that produced more than 50,000 insect specimens.

Many remained in museum collections for years before scientists had the opportunity to examine them closely.

Schroeder and her adviser, entomologist Christiane Weirauch , eventually studied hundreds of specimens borrowed from major natural history collections. Their research showed that the insects represented distinct species, even though they shared host plants and had similar physical characteristics.

The research also demonstrates why taxonomy remains important. Giving an organism a scientific identity allows researchers to study its biology, evolutionary relationships and ecological role. That information can ultimately help scientists understand and protect biodiversity.

Schroeder hopes the unusual connection will draw attention to the enormous number of insect species that haven’t yet been formally identified. Scientists believe vast numbers of insects remain undocumented, meaning discoveries like these are still possible even in collections containing specimens gathered decades ago.

The study describing the four Swiftiephylus species is part of a larger scientific paper documenting 12 newly described insects. Published in Insect Systematics & Evolution, the research adds another small piece to scientists’ understanding of Australia’s remarkable insect diversity.

While Swift is best known for stadium tours, blockbuster albums and a global fanbase, her newest namesakes are considerably smaller.

These Australian plant bugs may never perform on a stage or appear on a music chart, but they’ve gained a place in scientific history carrying the name of one of the world’s most recognizable entertainers.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes has separated himself from the NFL’s QBs in playoff success with a gap no one else is close to closing
articles.standfirst: Mahomes has 17 wins, followed by Aaron Rodgers with 12 playoff wins
articles.summary: Mahomes has 17 wins, followed by Aaron Rodgers with 12 playoff wins
articles.body:
The NFL season is back and for a second consecutive year Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers will be the oldest player. As he embarks on his farewell campaign, Rodgers joins Tom Brady as the only quarterbacks since 1950 to start Week 1 at age 42 or older. Brady ultimately played until he was 45, capturing a ring at age 43 with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2020 .

On the other side of the balance, no rookies will start in Week 1 , but five teams will feature a new signal-caller to begin the season, including Malik Willis in Miami, Geno Smith with the Jets, Kirk Cousins in Las Vegas, Kyler Murray in Minnesota, and Cooper Rush in Atlanta. Furthermore, only 10 of the 32 starting quarterbacks in Week 1 have been with their current teams for more than five seasons.

Patrick Mahomes Stands Alone Atop the Postseason Landscape

When evaluating the premier signal-callers gracing the gridiron this autumn, Patrick Mahomes from the Kansas City Chiefs rests on a tier entirely of his own regarding playoff success, not only for logging a staggering five Super Bowl appearances and capturing three rings, but also for racking up a division-leading 17 postseason victories .

The reality is that prior to last year's structural shifts, Mahomes had triumphed in at least one playoff game across all of his seven seasons as an entrenched starter, constantly anchoring his squad deep in the AFC Championship Game .

Consequently, the superstar passer approaches this fresh campaign fueled by competitive hunger, determined to steer his franchise right back into dominant winning ways.

Active Playoff Win Leaders Across the League

Trailing behind Mahomes' unmatched pace sits Aaron Rodgers with 11 postseason wins , making this elite tandem the only active field generals boasting more than 10 playoff victories.

Securing third place stands Josh Allen with 8 wins , followed closely by veteran Matthew Stafford with 7 victories in fourth, while Super Bowl 59 MVP Jalen Hurts holds fifth place holding 6 wins .

Rounding out the elite tier, Joe Burrow and Brock Purdy each command 5 postseason victories, completing the exclusive circle of contemporary quarterbacks who have accumulated five or more playoff triumphs as the league battles through another grueling championship chase.

articles.title: Andy Reid expects DT Chris Jones to play Week 1 vs. Broncos despite calf issue
articles.standfirst: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid remains optimistic about his defensive centerpiece despite a late calf problem
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid remains optimistic about his defensive centerpiece despite a late calf problem
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs appear likely to have Chris Jones available for their opening game of the 2026 NFL season despite a late injury concern involving the veteran defensive tackle.

Jones was added to Kansas City 's injury report Friday with a calf issue and was limited during practice. The development immediately raised questions about whether one of the Chiefs ' most important defensive players would be able to take the field against the Denver Broncos .

However, head coach Andy Reid has provided a positive update. According to reports from the Chiefs ' final preparations, Jones was held out of Saturday's practice after his calf tightened up Friday, but Reid did not sound overly concerned about the situation.

" Andy Reid said Chris Jones was held out of today's practice because his calf tightened up Friday. ‘I think he'll be all right,' Reid said of Jones ," Nate Taylor of ESPN reported.

Jones was still present at practice Saturday, although he did not wear a helmet. Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reported that the defensive tackle went through warmups and stretching while wearing a compression sleeve on his left calf.

" Chris Jones was out at practice Saturday but without a helmet. He had a compression sleeve on his left calf. He was going through warmups and stretch," Sweeney reported.

The Chiefs ' decision to be cautious with Jones is particularly understandable given that the team does not have to play until Monday night. The extra recovery time could give the 32-year-old more opportunity to make sure the calf is ready before he takes the field at Arrowhead Stadium.

The latest official injury information also provides encouragement. Jones was listed as limited on Friday but did not receive a game-status designation on the Chiefs ' final report, meaning Kansas City has not formally ruled him out or labeled him questionable for the matchup.

Jones remains central to Kansas City's defensive plans

There is little doubt why the Chiefs would prefer to have Jones available for the first game of the season.

The veteran has established himself as one of the NFL's premier interior defensive linemen since Kansas City selected him in the second round of the 2016 draft.

He enters his 11th season with the franchise and has accumulated 87.5 career sacks, which ranks among the best totals for defensive tackles since he entered the league.

Jones was also selected to his seventh Pro Bowl following the 2025 season. He finished that campaign with seven sacks and 29 combined tackles across 17 games, continuing an impressive run of production despite being one of the most heavily scrutinized players on opposing offensive lines.

His ability to collapse the pocket from the middle could be particularly valuable against Denver.

The Broncos enter the season with Bo Nix returning at quarterback, while Denver will be looking to build on a 2025 campaign in which the team ended Kansas City's long reign atop the AFC West. The Broncos are therefore not simply another Week 1 opponent for Reid's team.

Kansas City is also entering a pivotal season of its own. Patrick Mahomes is preparing to return from the knee injury that ended his 2025 campaign, and Reid has indicated that Mahomes is expected to start if there are no setbacks.

That makes the opening-night matchup especially important for a Chiefs team attempting to immediately reassert itself in the division.

Kansas City will already be without two starters, with Josh Simmons and Chamarri Conner ruled out for the opener. Keeping Jones on the field would therefore provide a significant boost to a defense that will have its hands full with Denver's offense.

The Chiefs and Broncos are scheduled to meet at Arrowhead Stadium on Monday, September 14, with kickoff set for 8:15 p.m. ET.

For now, Reid's assessment suggests the Chiefs are taking a precautionary approach rather than dealing with a major injury. If Jones continues progressing over the next two days, Kansas City should have its defensive anchor available when the AFC West rivals meet under the Monday night lights.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ backyard football field has an unexpected opponent and Brittany is showing the damage
articles.standfirst: A group of birds has turned the Mahomes’ home field into their personal playground
articles.summary: A group of birds has turned the Mahomes’ home field into their personal playground
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes is used to facing aggressive defenses, but the opponent attacking his family’s backyard might be the one he can’t beat. A group of eagles has been repeatedly pecking at the grass on the football field installed at their Kansas City-area home, and Brittany Mahomes is documenting the damage.

In a series of posts on her Instagram Stories, Brittany showed the birds scattered across the field, pecking at the turf and leaving visible marks behind. The mess didn’t stop at the playing surface. “They also destroyed all our blow-ups,” Brittany wrote, adding a smiling emoji that seemed to express frustration rather than amusement.

The Eagles keep coming back

The eagles first appeared around July , according to Brittany. By August, she thought they had left for good. “But sadly they left,” she wrote at the time. “I think they had their babies and now they’re gone they come back for mating season, maybe, I don’t know.” Her prediction turned out to be accurate: the birds returned, and this time they brought more damage.

For Mahomes , who spends his Sundays reading NFL defenses, this is a different kind of problem: no game plan, no blitz pickup, and no way to stop the birds from winning. While he prepares for another season with the Chiefs, Brittany is left to deal with the aftermath, one peck at a time. The backyard may be built for football, but right now, it belongs to the eagles.

For Mahomes, this is a different kind of problem than the ones he faces every Sunday. On the field, he knows how to read defenses and find solutions. In his own backyard, there is no play that works. Brittany is the one dealing with the mess while he gets ready for another season with the Chiefs. The football field is there for training, but for now, it belongs to the birds.

The Chiefs open their 2026 season on Monday, September 14, against the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium on Monday Night Football. It is a chance for Kansas City to bounce back after a disappointing 6-11 season in 2025, when Mahomes missed time with a season-ending knee injury.

Mahomes finished last year with 3,587 passing yards, 22 touchdowns, and 11 interceptions below his usual standard. He already holds the Chiefs' franchise records with 35,939 passing yards and 267 touchdown passes, and he enters 2026 with something to prove.
